{{Short description|Digital rights locker for films and TV programs}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=February 2014}}
[[File:Logo UltraViolet-DECE.svg|thumb|250x250px|UltraViolet logo]]
'''UltraViolet''' was a [[Cloud computing|cloud-based]] [[Digital rights management|digital rights]] [[digital locker|locker]] for films and television programs that allowed consumers to store proofs-of-purchase of licensed content in an account to enable playback on different devices using multiple applications from several different streaming services.<ref name=sixQs>{{cite web|last=Tribbey|first=Chris|title=Six Questions: Ultraviolet's Mitch Singer|url=http://www.homemediamagazine.com/electronic-delivery/six-questions-ultraviolet%E2%80%99s-mitch-singer-20510|work=Home Media Magazine|publisher=Questex Media Group|access-date=April 1, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717234132/http://www.homemediamagazine.com/electronic-delivery/six-questions-ultraviolet%E2%80%99s-mitch-singer-20510|archive-date=July 17, 2011|df=mdy-all}}</ref> UltraViolet also allowed users to share access to their library with up to five additional people. UltraViolet was deployed by the [[Digital Entertainment Content Ecosystem]] (DECE),<ref>{{cite web|title= UltraViolet/DECE Alliance Members| url= https://www.uvvu.com/en/us/uv-for-business| website= uvvu.com| url-status= dead| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140215191131/https://www.uvvu.com/en/us/uv-for-business| publisher= Digital Entertainment Content Ecosystem| archive-date= February 15, 2014| access-date= October 30, 2017}}</ref><ref name= "cnet everything">{{cite news| url= https://www.cnet.com/news/ultraviolet-everything-you-need-to-know/| title= UltraViolet video: Everything you need to know| first= Iyaz| last= Azhtar| website= [[CNET]].com| publisher= CBS Interactive |date= June 30, 2015| access-date= October 30, 2017}}</ref> an alliance of 85{{citation needed|date= October 2017}} companies that included [[film studio]]s, retailers, consumer electronics manufacturers, [[cable television]] companies, [[internet service provider]]s (ISPs), [[Internet hosting service|internet hosting]] vendors, and other systems and security vendors,<ref name="businesses">{{cite web |title=Participating UltraViolet Companies |url=https://www.myuv.com/ultraviolet-business |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170714022200/https://www.myuv.com/ultraviolet-business |archive-date=July 14, 2017 |access-date=October 30, 2017 |website=MyUV.com |publisher=Digital Entertainment Content Ecosystem}}</ref> with the notable exceptions of [[Walt Disney Studios (division)|Walt Disney Studios]], [[Google]], [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]], [[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer|MGM]], and [[Apple Inc.|Apple]].

On January 31, 2019, DECE announced that UltraViolet would shut down on July 31, 2019. This shutdown came after the launch of [[Movies Anywhere]] over a year earlier, along with Fox, Universal, Lionsgate, Paramount, and Warner Bros. beginning to drop out of issuing new UV rights for their films during that time period.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Roettgers |first=Janko |date=2019-01-30 |title=Ultraviolet Cloud Movie Locker to Shut Down (EXCLUSIVE) |url=https://variety.com/2019/digital/news/ultraviolet-shutting-down-1203123898/ |work=Variety}}</ref>

==Operation==
To use UltraViolet, consumers needed to create a free account, either through a participating UltraViolet service provider, or through the official website. An UltraViolet account was a digital rights locker where licenses (effectively receipts) for purchased content were stored and managed irrespective of the [[point of sale]]. The account holder was allowed to share their library with 5 other users, which were called members.

Consumers could acquire UltraViolet rights by purchasing a physical disc that included an UltraViolet activation code, by purchasing a movie directly from an electronic retailer (a.k.a. EST, or [[Electronic sell-through]]), or by using a '''disc to digital''' service (D2D). Disc to digital services allowed consumers to insert a DVD or [[Blu-ray]] into their computer's disc drive, scan it to verify ownership, and then add it to their UltraViolet collection for a fee. Several retailers including [[Vudu]] and [[CinemaNow]] offered this service. [[Flixster]] had been offering a D2D service as well, but it was suspended once [[Fandango (ticket service)|Fandango]] acquired Flixster in early 2016 and another independent [[Video on demand|movie streaming service]], M-GO.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Rotten Tomatoes and Flixster Acquired By Fandango|url = https://www.slashfilm.com/rotten-tomatoes-fandango-flixster/ |website = Slashfilm.com | date= February 17, 2016| first= Peter | last= Sciretta |access-date = October 30, 2017|language = en-US}}</ref>

Consumers could then stream or download their UltraViolet content from any participating retailer. Former participating retailers are listed in the table below.

The UltraViolet digital locker did not store video files, and was not a "cloud storage" platform. Only the rights for purchased content were stored on the service. UltraViolet only coordinated and managed the licenses for each account, but not the content itself. By creating a digital-rights locker rather than a digital media storage locker, UltraViolet bypassed the cost of storage and bandwidth used when the media is accessed and passed that cost on to various service providers.

==Content partners==
Five of the [[Major film studio|then "Big Six" major film studio]]s (now the "Big Five" since 2019) and [[Major film studio#Mini-majors|"mini-major"]] [[Lionsgate Films|Lionsgate]] were members of [[Digital Entertainment Content Ecosystem|DECE]], and released their content with UltraViolet rights.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alliance Members|url=http://www.uvvu.com/alliance-members.php|publisher=Digital Entertainment Content Ecosystem (DECE)|access-date=March 31, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120918223404/http://www.uvvu.com/alliance-members.php|archive-date=September 18, 2012|df=mdy-all}}</ref> Other minor film and television studios released their programming and movies with UltraViolet rights, but were not DECE members.

* Major film studios
** [[Sony Pictures Entertainment]] (films released for digital distribution before August 2019)
** [[Universal Pictures|Universal Studios]]  (films released for digital distribution before January 2018)
** [[Paramount Pictures]] (films released for digital distribution before December 2018)
** [[Warner Bros. Entertainment]] (films released for digital distribution before March 2019)
** [[Fox Entertainment Group]] (films released for digital distribution before December 2017; [[Acquisition of 21st Century Fox by Disney|studio's acquisition by Disney]] reduced the number of majors to five)
* Minor Film Studios
** [[Lionsgate Films|Lionsgate]] (films released for digital distribution before July 17, 2018)
** [[The Weinstein Company]] (films released for digital distribution before the company shut down in May 2018)
** [[Roadshow Entertainment]]
** [[Anchor Bay Entertainment|Anchor Bay]] (films released for digital distribution before the company shut down in 2017)
** [[DreamWorks Animation]] (films released for digital distribution before October 2017; studio previously purchased and acquired by [[Universal Pictures|Universal]])
* Television Studios
** [[BBC]]
** [[HBO]]

Despite Fox merging with Disney in 2019, Walt Disney Studios was never a member of DECE, and did not release any of their films with UltraViolet rights. On February 25, 2014, Disney launched a competing digital movie locker system called [[Movies Anywhere#History|Disney Movies Anywhere]] that allowed any Disney movie purchased or redeemed at any participating provider to be played using all other DMA providers. DMA providers included iTunes, Vudu, Google Play, Amazon Video, and Microsoft Movies & TV. On October 12, 2017, Disney Movies Anywhere was expanded to include movies from a number of non-Disney studios, thus forming a full-fledged UltraViolet competitor. This service is now called [[Movies Anywhere]] to reflect the expanded scope of content.

==UltraViolet digital retailers==
UltraViolet content was available from several movie streaming services.<ref>{{cite web|title=UV Demystified|url=http://www.uvdemystified.com/uvfaq.html#1.7.1|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110416025027/http://www.uvdemystified.com/uvfaq.html#1.7.1|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 16, 2011}}</ref> Some services offered downloads that could be saved to PCs, tablets, gaming consoles, or phones for offline viewing. Below is a table of all the streaming providers and the countries they serve.

Content could also be streamed over the Internet to an unlimited number of devices, depending on the content license rights held by the streaming provider.<ref name=variety>{{cite news|last=Graser|first=Marc|title=Hollywood clicks with UltraViolet digital locker|url=https://variety.com/2011/digital/news/hollywood-clicks-with-ultraviolet-digital-locker-1118029799/|access-date=April 1, 2011|newspaper=Variety|date=January 5, 2011}}</ref>

==Download capability==
Some Ultraviolet streaming providers offered the capability to download movies and TV shows. They had their own proprietary video formats, and they were not cross-platform. They had to be downloaded and played within their own proprietary PC, Mac, iOS, or Android apps.

The Ultraviolet Common File Format (CFF) was planned, but never launched. The CFF was an attempt by the DECE to allow downloaded video files to be copied between devices, stored on physical media (e.g. DVDs, [[SD card]]s, [[flash memory]]) or online backup services. They were intended to be playable on any UltraViolet authorized device (e.g. Blu-ray, streaming media player, Smart TV', or mobile device) or software player registered to the household Ultraviolet library.

A 2015 simplification of the UV ecosystem made the Common File Format optional for studios and streaming providers. CFF was never supported by any retailers nor was it ever released to a consumer audience.

==Selected DRM technologies==

UltraViolet Streaming providers were free to choose whatever [[Digital rights management|DRM technologies]] they wanted to use for streaming and downloads.

[[DECE]] approved six [[Digital rights management|DRM technologies]] for use in conjunction with the proposed common file format, which was never launched.

The selected DRM technologies were:
* Google [[Widevine]] DRM, chosen for its strong position on set-top boxes
* [[Marlin (DRM)|Marlin DRM]], chosen for its compatibility with many [[Connected TV]]s
* OMA [[OMA DRM|CMLA-OMA v2]], chosen for its strong position on mobile devices
* Microsoft [[PlayReady]], chosen for its wide availability on PC and CE devices
* Adobe Primetime DRM, chosen for its wide availability on PC devices
* DivX DRM<ref>{{Cite web|date=7 January 2013|title=DivX Plus Streaming DRM Approved for UltraViolet Services|url=http://www.rovicorp.com/company/press-releases/2013/1/7/divx-plus-str-drm-approved-for-ultraviolet-services.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150119170054/http://www.rovicorp.com/company/press-releases/2013/1/7/divx-plus-str-drm-approved-for-ultraviolet-services.html|archive-date=19 January 2015|access-date=2020-11-12}}</ref>

==History==

===2010===

In September, Mitch Singer, the President of [[Digital Entertainment Content Ecosystem|DECE]], announced the upcoming launch of the "UltraViolet" system in an interview with Home Media Magazine.<ref>{{cite web|title=Six Questions: Ultraviolet's Mitch Singer|url=http://www.homemediamagazine.com/electronic-delivery/six-questions-ultraviolet%E2%80%99s-mitch-singer-20510|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717234132/http://www.homemediamagazine.com/electronic-delivery/six-questions-ultraviolet%E2%80%99s-mitch-singer-20510|archive-date=July 17, 2011|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

===2011===

In January, a number of major film studios announced support for UltraViolet. They were: Warner Bros, Sony Pictures, Fox, Universal, Paramount, and Lionsgate. The notable exception was Walt Disney.<ref>{{cite web|last=Tribbey|first=Chris|date=5 January 2011|title=UltraViolet Gets Studio Support|url=http://www.homemediamagazine.com/digital-copy/ultraviolet-gets-studio-support-21611|website=HomeMedia Magazine}}</ref>

On October 11, the UltraViolet system launched with the [[Warner Bros]] release of ''[[Horrible Bosses]]'', the first UV title. [[Flixster]] re-launched as the first UltraViolet streaming service.<ref>{{cite web|last=Duncan|first=Geoff|date=12 October 2011|title=UltraViolet Soft Launches with Horrible Bosses|url=http://www.digitaltrends.com/home-theater/ultraviolet-soft-launches-with-horrible-bosses|website=Digital Trends}}</ref> [[Sony]] subsequently released its first two UV titles in December, ''[[The Smurfs (film)|The Smurfs]]'' and ''[[Friends with Benefits (film)|Friends with Benefits]]''.<ref>{{cite web|last=Tribbey|first=Chris|date=20 September 2011|title='The Smurfs,' 'Friends With Benefits' First UltraViolet Titles for Sony|url=http://www.homemediamagazine.com/sony-pictures/the-smurfs-friends-with-benefits-first-ultraviolet-titles-sony-25114|website=HomeMedia Magazine}}</ref> [[Universal Pictures|Universal]] soon followed with the release of its first UV title, ''[[Cowboys & Aliens]]''.<ref>{{cite web|last=Tribbey|first=Chris|date=8 December 2011|title=UltraViolet Titles Keep Coming, With More Details Due At CES|url=http://www.homemediamagazine.com/digital-copy/ultraviolet-titles-keep-coming-with-more-details-due-ces-25835|website=HomeMedia Magazine}}</ref>

In December, UltraViolet launched in the UK with the Warner Bros release of ''[[Final Destination 5]]''.<ref>{{cite web|last=Tartaglione|first=Nancy|date=8 December 2011|title='Final Destination 5′ Is First For UltraViolet In The UK; Will British Users Have Clearer Picture Than In The U.S.?|url=https://deadline.com/2011/12/final-destination-5-is-first-for-ultraviolet-in-the-uk-will-british-users-have-clearer-picture-than-in-the-u-s-202665/|website=Deadline}}</ref>

===2012===

At the [[Consumer Electronics Show]] in January, [[Amazon.com|Amazon]] became the first major retailer to announce support for UltraViolet.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Ingraham|first=Nathan|date=2012-01-10|title=Amazon is UltraViolet's first retail partner; Samsung offering disc-to-digital on 2012 Blu-Ray players|url=https://www.theverge.com/2012/1/10/2697997/amazon-ultraviolet-retail-partner-samsung-disc-to-digital|access-date=2020-11-16|website=The Verge|language=en}}</ref> The DEG reported that 750k accounts had been created in the first 3 months.<ref>{{cite web|last=Giardina|first=Carolyn|date=10 January 2012|title=UltraViolet Registration Surges In First Three Months|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/dece-more-750000-households-register-280324|website=The Hollywood Reporter}}</ref>

In January, [[Paramount Pictures|Paramount]] released its first UV title "Paranormal Activity 3" <ref>{{cite web|last=Gunther|first=Richard|date=24 January 2012|title=Paramount Introduces UltraViolet Titles While Fox Waits|url=http://thedigitalmediazone.com/2012/01/24/paramount-introduces-ultraviolet-titles-while-fox-waits/|publisher=The Digital Media Zone}}</ref> and in April [[DreamWorks Animation]] became the seventh studio to join the UltraViolet initiative with "Shrek", "Madagascar", "Kung Fu Panda" and "How to Train Your Dragon".<ref>{{cite web|last=Giardina|first=Carolyn|date=15 April 2012|title=Dreamworks Animation Teams with Wal-Mart's Disc to Digital Service|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/dreamworks-animation-walmart-disc-digital-312298|website=The Hollywood Report}}</ref> Also in April, [[Vudu]] (operated by [[Walmart]]) became the first major UltraViolet retailer by adding UV rights to thousands of films. Walmart also launched an in-store "Disc to Digital" service, with more than 4,000 titles initially.<ref>{{cite web|last=Tribbey|first=Chris|date=11 April 2012|title=4,000-Plus Titles Available in Walmart Disc-to-Digital Program|url=http://www.homemediamagazine.com/walmart/4000-plus-titles-available-walmart-disc-digital-program-26945|website=HomeMedia Magazine}}</ref>

Between August and September, [[Lionsgate Films|Lionsgate]] and [[20th Century Fox]] released their first titles on UV.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gruenwedel|first=Erik|date=10 August 2012|title=Lionsgate Makes "Hunger Games" its First UltraViolet Release|url=http://www.homemediamagazine.com/lionsgate/lionsgate-makes-hunger-games-its-first-ultraviolet-release-28047|website=HomeMedia Magazine}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Kit|first=Borys|date=18 September 2012|title=Fox Home Entertainment Launches Digital HD Prometheus|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/fox-home-entertainment-launches-digital-hd-prometheus-371157|website=The Hollywood Reporter}}</ref> UltraViolet surpassed 5 million users and 7,200 titles on September 20.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Lang|first1=Brent|last2=Shaw|first2=Lucas|date=20 September 2012|title=Is UltraViolet Finally Ready to Save Hollywood's Day?|url=https://www.thewrap.com/media/article/ultraviolet-finally-ready-save-hollywoods-day-57051|website=The Wrap|access-date=February 18, 2020|archive-date=December 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181211010233/https://www.thewrap.com/media/article/ultraviolet-finally-ready-save-hollywoods-day-57051/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

[[Redbox]] announced a partnership with UltraViolet for its new Redbox Instant streaming service on October 25. Ultraviolet support never materialized, and the service shut down on October 7, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|date=25 October 2012|title=Redbox Will Promote UltraViolet In New Disc And Online Deal With Warner Bros|url=https://deadline.com/2012/10/redbox-will-promote-ultraviolet-in-new-disc-deal-with-warner-bros-359867/|website=Deadline}}</ref>

On October 30, [[Barnes & Noble]] announced it would launch an UltraViolet enabled electronic video store for its new [[Nook HD]] tablet.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rigg|first=Jamie|date=30 October 2012|title=Barnes & Noble bolstering Nook Video catalogue, bringing UltraViolet to the HD and HD+|url=https://www.engadget.com/2012/10/30/nook-video-catalogue-expansion/|website=Engadget}}</ref>

[[Best Buy]]'s CinemaNow became the second major UV retailer on November 24.<ref>{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Mat|date=24 November 2012|title=CinemaNow adds Ultraviolet support to some of its movies|url=https://www.engadget.com/2012/11/24/cinemanow-adds-ultraviolet-support-to-some-of-its-movies-vod/|website=Engadget}}</ref> [[CinemaNow]] launched an in-home Disc to Digital service (in beta) in December.<ref>{{cite web|last=Lawler|first=Richard|date=20 December 2012|title=Best Buy's CinemaNow opens home disc-to-digital program, makes cloud copies of DVDs for a fee|url=https://www.engadget.com/2012/12/20/best-buys-cinemanow-kicks-home-disc-to-digital-program-gives-d/|website=Engadget}}</ref>

===2013===

In January, [[DreamWorks Animation]] and [[Technicolor]] launched M-GO, a new streaming platform with UV capability,<ref>{{cite web|last=Lawler|first=Richard|date=5 January 2013|title=M-GO video on-demand movie service launches, streams to PCs, Samsung and Vizio players|url=https://www.engadget.com/2013/01/05/m-go-video-on-demand-movie-service-launches-streams-to-pcs-sam/|website=Engadget}}</ref> and [[Cineplex Entertainment|Cineplex]] became the first UltraViolet retailer in Canada.<ref>{{cite web|last=Mann|first=Colin|date=January 2013|title=Cineplex debuts UltaViolet in Canada|url=http://advanced-television.info/2013/01/11/cineplex-debuts-ultraviolet-in-canada/|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130112062458/http://advanced-television.info/2013/01/11/cineplex-debuts-ultraviolet-in-canada/|archive-date=12 January 2013}}</ref>

In April, [[Best Buy]] announced a deal to make its UV ready Cinema Now service available in Canada.<ref>{{cite web|last=O'Rourke|first=Patrick|date=25 April 2013|title=UltraViolet and CinemaNow Announce a New Partnership|url=http://o.canada.com/technology/personal-tech/ultraviolet-and-cinemanow-announce-a-new-partnership/|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131112142205/http://o.canada.com/technology/personal-tech/ultraviolet-and-cinemanow-announce-a-new-partnership/|archive-date=12 November 2013}}</ref> In May, UltraViolet launched in Australia and New Zealand,<ref>{{cite web|last=Sakr|first=Sharif|date=17 April 2013|title=The Hobbit will be first movie to support UltraViolet in New Zealand and Australia|url=https://www.engadget.com/2013/04/17/the-hobbit-will-be-first-movie-to-support-ultraviolet-in-new-zea/|website=Engadget}}</ref> [[Kaleidescape]] opened a UV ready video download store,<ref>{{cite web|last=Lawler|first=Richard|date=2 May 2013|title=Kaleidescape's online video store officially opens, promises Blu-ray quality downloads|url=https://www.engadget.com/2013/05/02/kaleidescape-store-launches-blu-ray-quality-downloads-ultraviolet/|website=Engadget}}</ref> and 20th Century Fox announced it would offer Digital HD UltraViolet rights with all new films.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kleist|first=Jeff|date=9 May 2013|title=Fox Offering Early Digital Access on New Titles, Cuts Out iTunes|url=http://www.technologytell.com/hometech/96212/fox-offering-digital-early/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140112102806/http://www.technologytell.com/hometech/96212/fox-offering-digital-early/|archive-date=12 January 2014}}</ref>

In September, CinemaNow launched its Disc to Digital service in Canada.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gruenwedel|first=Erik|date=12 September 2013|title=CinemaNow Bows Disc to Digital in Canada|url=http://www.homemediamagazine.com/best-buy/cinemanow-bows-disc-digital-canada-31363|website=HomeMedia Magazine}}</ref> and Target Ticket launched with UltraViolet capability.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gruenwedel|first=Erik|date=25 September 2013|title=Target launches Digital Content Store with UltraViolet|url=http://www.homemediamagazine.com/target/target-launches-digital-content-store-ultraviolet-31457|website=HomeMedia Magazine}}</ref> Ultraviolet expanded to France, Germany, Austria, and Switzerland in November.

===2014===

In January, [[Digital Entertainment Content Ecosystem|DECE]] launched a revamped UltraViolet website with new features.<ref>{{cite web|title=New UltraViolet launches, lets you delete movies|url=http://www.technologytell.com/hometech/104457/new-ultraviolet-launches-enables-deleting-movies/|publisher=Technology Tell|access-date=May 20, 2014|archive-date=March 20, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140320071947/http://www.technologytell.com/hometech/104457/new-ultraviolet-launches-enables-deleting-movies/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On February 25, Disney launched [[Movies Anywhere|Disney Movies Anywhere]], a streaming service.<ref>{{cite web|title=Disney Movies Anywhere service launches with an unprecedented link to iTunes|date=February 25, 2014 |url=https://www.engadget.com/2014/02/25/disney-movies-anywhere/}}</ref> The next day, Mitch Singer, the President of DECE, stated that the new Disney Movies Anywhere service would not prohibit Disney from offering UltraViolet titles in the future.<ref>{{cite web|title=UltraViolet exec reacts to Disney Movies Anywhere launch |url=http://kidscreen.com/2014/02/26/ultraviolet-exec-reacts-to-disney-movies-anywhere-launch/|publisher=iKids}}</ref>

At the end of March, Vudu became the first UV retailer to offer [[Google]] [[Chromecast]] support for UltraViolet content.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cast Away Today with Vudu for Chromecast|url=http://blog.vudu.com/?p=10872|access-date=April 11, 2014|archive-date=April 1, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140401210841/http://blog.vudu.com/?p=10872|url-status=dead}}</ref> Flixster also became a retailer for UV in March.<ref>{{cite web|title=Flixster movies app adds Chromecast support|url=http://www.androidcentral.com/flixster-movies-app-adds-chromecast-support|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407185153/http://www.androidcentral.com/flixster-movies-app-adds-chromecast-support|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 7, 2014}}</ref>

In May, Vudu introduced a new feature that allowed UltraViolet users to share their movies with up to five friends.<ref>{{cite web|title=Walmart's Vudu Now Allows UltraViolet Users To Share Their Movies With Up To Five Friends| date=May 14, 2014 |url=https://techcrunch.com/2014/05/14/vudu-ultraviolet-sharing/?ncid=rss|publisher=Techcrunch}}</ref> Also in May, Flixster became the first UV retailer to support Apple [[Airplay]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Flixster Movies App Gets AirPlay Support|date=May 21, 2014 |url=http://www.iclarified.com/40937/flixster-movies-app-gets-airplay-support}}</ref>

In October [[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer|MGM]] began to offer UV rights for several of its catalog titles. Also in October, Tesco's [[Blinkbox|BlinkBox]] became the first official UV retailer in the U.K.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tesco now offers digital copies of movies you've bought in any store|url=https://www.engadget.com/2014/10/14/tesco-blinkbox-ultraviolet-movies/|website=engadget|date=October 14, 2014 }}</ref>

On Nov. 12, KnowHow, a UK streaming movie provider, relaunched as CinemaNow and added Ultraviolet support.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Colin|first1=Mann|title=Knowow relaunches as CinemaNow, adds UltraViolet|url=http://advanced-television.com/2014/11/12/knowhow-movies-relaunches-as-cinemanow-adds-ultraviolet/|website=Advanced Television|date=November 12, 2014 }}</ref> Also in November [[Verizon FiOS|Verizon FIOS]] on Demand introduced UltraViolet capability.<ref>{{cite web|title=UltraViolet Says It Will Continue To Grow, Even Without Disney And Amazon|url=https://deadline.com/2014/12/ultraviolet-growth-disney-amazon-1201326125/|website=Deadline|date=December 16, 2014 }}</ref>

===2015===

On January 6, The DEG announced that UltraViolet grew 30% in 2014 to 21 million accounts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Digital Growth, Weak Box Office Further Eroded Consumer Spending on Disc in 2014|url=http://www.homemediamagazine.com/research/digital-growth-weak-box-office-further-eroded-consumer-spending-disc-2014-34920}}</ref>

French supermarket chain Carrefour opened a digital video store with UltraViolet functionality called Nolim Films on January 27.<ref>{{cite web|title=French Supermarket Chain Carrefour Bows Digital Video Store; Gets First UltraViolet Functionality|date=January 27, 2015 |url=http://www.homemediamagazine.com/retailers/french-supermarket-chain-carrefour-bows-digital-video-store-gets-first-ultraviolet}}</ref>

Target Corporation shut down its Target Ticket service on March 7, and allowed users to transfer their purchases to CinemaNow and Disney Movies Anywhere.<ref>{{cite web|title=Target Ticket|url=http://www.targetticket.com/|access-date=October 9, 2013|archive-date=October 4, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004000127/http://www.targetticket.com/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

UltraViolet surpassed 22 million users on May 25.<ref>{{cite web|title=Digital Goes Over the Top|date=May 24, 2015 |url=http://www.homemediamagazine.com/news/digital-goes-over-top-35916|publisher=Home Media Magazine}}</ref>

Australian UV Partner EZYFlix.tv closed down on August 18.<ref>{{cite web|title=Aussie Digital Movie Service EzyFlix Ceases Operations|date=August 18, 2015 |url=http://www.homemediamagazine.com/vod/aussie-digital-movie-service-ezyflix-ceases-operations-36481}}</ref>

===2016===
On Jan 6, The DEG reported that UltraViolet accounts grew by almost 20 percent in 2015 to hit more than 25 million with 165 million movies and television shows in UltraViolet libraries.<ref>{{cite web|title=DEG: Home-Video Spending Up 1% In 2015|url=http://www.twice.com/news/statistics/deg-home-video-spending-1-2015/59982|website=Twice.com|date=January 6, 2016 }}</ref>

On January 29, Fandango acquired the M-GO movie service, and planned to re-launch it later that year under a new name.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fandango Acquires M-GO Movie Service from Dreamworks Animation And Technicolor|url=https://variety.com/2016/digital/news/fandango-acquires-m-gg-movie-service-from-dreamworks-animation-and-technicolor-1201692324/|website=Variety|date=January 29, 2016 }}</ref>

On March 3, Barnes and Noble announced that it would shutter its Nook Video Store on March 15.<ref>{{cite web|title=Barnes & Noble is shutting down the Nook App Store on March 15th|date=March 4, 2016 |url=https://www.theverge.com/2016/3/4/11160942/barnes-noble-nook-app-store-shutting-down-march-15th|publisher=The Verge}}</ref>

On March 30, M-GO became Fandango Now and launched Airplay support.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fandango Rebrands M-GO On-Demand Video Service As FandangoNOW|url=https://deadline.com/2016/03/fandango-launches-fandangonow-vod-service-1201721301/|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=March 16, 2016 }}</ref>

On April 4, BlinkBox —owned by TalkTalk— stopped supporting the PlayStation 3.<ref>{{cite web|title=Blinkbox TalkTalk TV changes to supported devices|url=https://support.blinkbox.com/hc/en-gb/articles/217191128}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

On June 29, an update was released for the [[Nvidia Shield]] Android TV console that enabled support for the Vudu app. Vudu became the first UltraViolet service available on the popular device.<ref>{{cite web|title=VUDU Android TV App Now Available On NVIDIA SHIELD|url=http://www.androidheadlines.com/2016/06/vudu-android-tv-app-now-available-on-nvidia-shield.html|website=Android Headlines|date=June 29, 2016 }}</ref>

On Sept 1, the Cineplex Store stopped offering Ultraviolet services.

===2017===
On March 20, JB Hi-Fi NOW Video service announced that it would close on 13 April 2017.

On March 23, Vudu expanded its Disc to Digital service. Users could now convert their movie library using the Vudu app on a mobile phone.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.engadget.com/2017/03/23/vudus-mobile-app-rips-digital-copies-of-your-blu-rays/ |title= Vudu's Mobile App Rips Digital Copies of Your Blu-Rays |website=Engadget|date= July 19, 2019 |publisher=AOL Tech}}</ref> They also announced that the in-store Disc to Digital program would be suspended on April 1.

As of March 27, UltraViolet accounts grew to 28 million.<ref>{{cite web|title=castLabs Builds New UltraViolet Central System for DECE|date=March 27, 2017 |url=http://castlabs.com/news/castlabs-ultraviolet-central-system/}}</ref>

In April, it was noticed that movies from [[Relativity Media]] that were distributed by [[20th Century Fox]], were no longer UV enabled. If you had purchased/redeemed the movie prior to the removal of UV rights, the movie remained in your UV locker.

In late May, Universal Studios began referring to UltraViolet as only "Digital HD" on the back of its Blu-ray releases. 20th Century Fox started this practice in 2016. Both studios films were still UltraViolet enabled at select retailers.

On July 1, it was reported that UltraViolet surpassed 30 million users.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.uvdemystified.com/uvfaq.html#7.1|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110416025027/http://www.uvdemystified.com/uvfaq.html#7.1|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 16, 2011|title=UltraViolet FAQ|last=Taylor|first=Jim|website=www.uvdemystified.com|language=en|access-date=2017-10-26}}</ref>

In mid-July, CinemaNow removed UV support for all movies. Questions to UltraViolet were answered with the response, "CinemaNow is not participating in UV at this time."

On August 1, the CinemaNow website began redirecting to Filmon.tv, a Live TV streaming service in the UK.

On August 21, U.S. Flixster Video announced "As of August 28, 2017, Flixster Video will no longer support code redemptions or streaming and downloading of content. Redeem codes and access your Flixster video collection after that date by signing up or logging into Vudu or FandangoNOW."

On August 22, Vudu launched their AppleTV app, which became the first app to support UltraViolet movies and TV shows on the Apple TV platform.<ref>{{cite web|title=VUDU App Officially Launches on Apple TV|url=https://www.macrumors.com/2017/08/22/vudu-app-apple-tv/|website=Macrumors.com|date=August 22, 2017 }}</ref>

On October 12, 2017, it was announced that [[Movies Anywhere|Disney Movies Anywhere]] would expand to include non-Disney studios under the name '''Movies Anywhere''', with 20th Century Fox, Sony Pictures, Universal, and Warner Bros. joining Disney as initial partners, and [[Lionsgate Studios|Lionsgate]] and [[Paramount Pictures]] expressing interest.

On November 28, digital releases of ''[[Detroit (film)|Detroit]]'' and ''[[Patti Cake$]]'' were the last films released by [[20th Century Fox Home Entertainment]] to receive UV rights, while ''[[Kingsman: The Golden Circle]]'' was the first to be released without UV rights.

===2018===
January 2, the first U.S. digital releases of 2018 from [[Universal Pictures]] were released without UV rights. Joining [[20th Century Fox]] as the second studio to drop UV rights for new releases.

From 15 January 2018 the Ultraviolet service was no longer available on TalkTalk TV.<ref>{{cite web|title=UltraViolet on TalkTalk TV Store|url=https://support.blinkbox.com/hc/en-gb/articles/202529856-UltraViolet-on-TalkTalk-TV-Store|access-date=January 22, 2018|archive-date=January 23, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180123072155/https://support.blinkbox.com/hc/en-gb/articles/202529856-UltraViolet-on-TalkTalk-TV-Store|url-status=dead}}</ref>

March 13 - FandangoNow joined MoviesAnywhere, and stopped offering UV rights for MA affiliated studios' films.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.engadget.com/2018/03/13/movies-anywhere-includes-your-fandangonow-flicks/|title=Movies Anywhere includes your FandangoNOW flicks|last=England|first=Rachel|date=2018-03-13|website=Engadget|access-date=2019-04-26}}</ref>

July 11, Twentieth Century Fox stopped issuing UV rights for all new purchases for catalog titles that were previously UV enabled.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://forum.vudu.com/forum/vudu/general-discussion/466485-fox-uv-status-change-effective-07-11-18|title=Fox UV Status Change Effective 07/11/18|access-date=December 10, 2018|archive-date=July 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180711224034/https://forum.vudu.com/forum/vudu/general-discussion/466485-fox-uv-status-change-effective-07-11-18|url-status=dead}}</ref>

July 17, Lionsgate titles released on or after July 17, 2018, would no longer be available on UltraViolet.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://forum.vudu.com/forum/vudu/general-discussion/470757-lionsgate-officially-out-of-uv-for-any-titles-released-after-july-17th-2018|title=Lionsgate officially out of UV for any titles released after July 17th 2018|date=August 21, 2018 }}</ref>

Sept 18, Universal Studios stopped issuing UV rights for all new purchases for catalog titles that were previously UV enabled.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://forum.vudu.com/forum/vudu/general-discussion/471810-universal-studios-uv-status-change-effective-09-18-18|title=Universal Studios UV Status Change Effective 09/18/18|access-date=December 10, 2018|archive-date=September 20, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180920045827/https://forum.vudu.com/forum/vudu/general-discussion/471810-universal-studios-uv-status-change-effective-09-18-18|url-status=dead}}</ref>

December 11, 2018, Paramount stopped issuing UV rights for all new releases moving forward. One week after, the final UV title was released with ''[[Mission: Impossible – Fallout]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://forum.vudu.com/forum/vudu/general-discussion/487552-issue-paramount-uhd-titles-no-uhd-uv-rights-tmnt-star-trek-beyond-g-i-joe|title=Paramount 4K UHD Titles - No UHD UV Licenses Issued|date=January 9, 2019 }}</ref>

===2019===
On January 30, [[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] reported that [[Digital Entertainment Content Ecosystem|DECE]] would shut down [[UltraViolet (system)|UltraViolet]] on July 31, 2019, with DECE officially confirming the news the next day.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://variety.com/2019/digital/news/ultraviolet-shutting-down-1203123898/ |title=Ultraviolet Cloud Movie Locker to Shut Down (EXCLUSIVE) | website= [[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |first= Janko| last=  Roettgers| date= 2019-01-30}}</ref> Users that had at least one major retailer, like [[Vudu]], connected to their UV account would be able to maintain streaming rights to movies and TV shows redeemed via the platform through those retailers.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://variety.com/2019/digital/news/ultraviolet-shutting-down-1203123898/ |title=Ultraviolet Cloud Movie Locker to Shut Down (EXCLUSIVE) | website= [[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |first= Janko| last=  Roettgers| date= 2019-01-30}}</ref>

On January 31, Sony Pictures Store shut down its website and discontinued all related operations in the U.S. except for their ULTRA 4K app.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.sonypicturesstore.com/ |title=Sony Pictures Stores - Shutdown Notice}}</ref>

On March 4, Verizon ended the linking of any additional Fios accounts with UltraViolet. Existing Fios accounts already linked to UltraViolet were not affected.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.verizon.com/Ondemand/Mylibrary/UltraViolet |title=UltraViolet FAQs - Fios TV Verizon}}</ref>

On March 13, Warner Bros. stopped issuing UV rights for all new purchases of catalog titles that had previously been UV enabled.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://forum.vudu.com/forum/vudu/general-discussion/496462-warner-bros-uv-status-change-effective-03-13-19 |title= Warner Bros UV Status Change Effective 03/13/19 |access-date= March 13, 2019 |archive-date= March 27, 2019 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20190327091532/https://forum.vudu.com/forum/vudu/general-discussion/496462-warner-bros-uv-status-change-effective-03-13-19 |url-status= dead }}</ref>

On March 18, Paramount Pictures issued a notice that the ability to rent, buy, or playback films via ParamountMovies.com would cease effective immediately. Additionally, redemption of digital copies began redirecting users to either Vudu or FandangoNow.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.paramountmovies.com/#/support |title=Paramount Movies - Support}}</ref>

On March 27, Verizon ended UltraViolet services on Fios. Titles that had previously imported into Fios library via UltraViolet remained unaffected.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.verizon.com/Ondemand/Mylibrary/UltraViolet |title=UltraViolet FAQs - Fios TV Verizon}}</ref>

On April 18, Sony Pictures informed customers via email and directly via the ULTRA 4K app that effective immediately new account sign-up, purchase, and redeem functions were to be removed from its TV and Windows apps. Customers could still use the ULTRA 4K app to stream films and TV shows in their UV library.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.sonypicturesstore.com/ |title=Sony Pictures - IMPORTANT ULTRA ACCOUNT NOTICE - NO ACTION REQUIRED }}</ref>

On May 31, 2019, Kaleidescape disconnected from UltraViolet. Any titles purchased at other retailers that had previously imported from UltraViolet remained in the Kaleidescape library.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.kaleidescape.com/movie-store/help#ultraviolet_shutdown/ |title= Kaleidescape FAQ - Is UltraViolet shutting down? |access-date= May 31, 2019 |archive-date= August 9, 2020 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20200809130640/https://www.kaleidescape.com/movie-store/help#ultraviolet_shutdown/ |url-status= dead }}</ref>

On July 26, 2019, Flixster Video informed its non-US subscribers by email of the impending UV shutdown on July 31, 2019. Flixster Video assured its subscribers that the shutdown of UltraViolet would not impact the titles already in the subscribers' Flixster collection. Flixster Video also went on to announce of its own shutdown late in 2019 (a date was not mentioned) and that arrangements had been made with Google Play to enable migration of available videos on subscribers' Flixster account to Google Play. They mentioned that they had expected the migration process to be available in July, but was not ready yet.

On July 31, the Ultraviolet website was available for the last time for subscribers. The website was closed on the next day on August 1, 2019.

On September 24, 2019, Flixster Video informed its non-US subscribers by email that it was planning to shut down its website, applications and operations on December 18, 2019. In the email, Flixster Video also announced that the arrangement for transfer of subscribers' videos to Google Play was ready. A link to start the migration process to Google Play was embedded in the email. Flixster's website provided information and instructions about migrating to Google Play. Flixster urged subscribers to complete the migration process to Google Play as soon as possible. They also mentioned that playback of subscribers videos would still be available through Flixster video until shutdown.

After the demise of Ultraviolet, current Paramount releases with a digital code have featured a portal on Paramount's home entertainment website where a choice of retailer redemption can be made (usually either iTunes, Google Play Movies/YouTube or Vudu), while Lionsgate currently requires the download of an app and requires the reception of their newsletter list via email to confirm the ownership of a title before the choice of retailer redemption is made; MGM films often depend on the actual home video distributor contracted by MGM to release each individual film (although some MGM films like ''[[Missing Link (2019 film)|Missing Link]]'' and ''[[Booksmart]]'' also end up in Movies Anywhere, usually through [[20th Century Fox Home Entertainment]]).

On October 1, FandangoNOW completed transferring over UV titles to users' regular Movies and TV libraries and removed the Ultraviolet links from their website and apps.
